correctness.rationale: For every unequal tuple in scope, an inward force at depth a+k sees neither the hub nor another arm, and a is the least depth it sees. Once the first m−1 arms are black, their depth-k vertex forces the hub; the shallower forcers expose successively depths 1 through k−1 on the last arm, the hub forces depth k, and within-arm forces proceed outward. Every pair of depths a≤b with b−a≤k is covered by a window starting at max(1,b−k), even at an end or at length k+1. The Gram block is therefore exactly supported on the required within-arm pairs; the nonnegative threshold couplings neither cancel entries nor introduce false edges. The zero-sum window recurrence permits arbitrary first k coordinates on each arm. Choosing their sum to be zero makes the hub and all threshold-block contributions vanish, giving (m−1)k independent null vectors. For any exact-support matrix, restriction of its kernel to a forcing set is injective by the forcing-row equations. This proves equality and the rank formula. Independent replay: python3 /workspace/spider_power_check.py; BFS power, exact rational rank and forcing closure agreed at (4,4,5), k=3; (5,7,11), k=4; (9,9,9,10), k=8; all size-five initial sets were also excluded in the first case. The reproduction is bounded; the written argument handles the full quantifier. Uploaded scripts were inspected, not run.
residual_risks: No conclusion for shorter arms or trees with additional branch vertices; no formal verification was performed.
